name: She and Her Tree Hole

lore:
Zvil never liked Vivian. She hated everything about her big sister, from her boring name, to the fact that she'd had the nerve to be born a few years earlier, let alone her utterly detestable two-faced personality.

Zvil couldn't understand how she had ended up with a sister like that. Now and then, after a particularly grueling bout of socializing, Zvil would hear Vivian muttering and grumbling behind her bedroom door. But most of the time, Vivian was so very, very kind and gentle to everyone. Everyone except Zvil.

"Zvil, my darling little sister."

Vivian plucked her out of the tree hollow with one hand. Zvil thrashed about like a jumping spider that had made some poor life choices and was waving every leg it had in protest. Red-faced with humiliation and rage, she twisted round and shrieked.

"I'm never going to those boring lessons again! Not one more word! You're the oldest and the cleverest anyway. I'll end up in some tiny fief, living in some shabby tree hollow, spending my whole life eating, playing in the mud, and sleeping. So why not start now?"

"You can't throw a tantrum just because you haven't learned as much at your age as I had at mine. And you certainly can't steal my life's ambition."

Zvil's eyes went very wide.

"Hiding in a tree hollow is MY plan. You've been fascinated by tax decrees and laws since you were four. How much of your clothing allowance do you secretly spend on the common folk every year? You truly love them. I truly can't stand them."

"And don't think I'll play favorites. If my siblings want that ridiculously heavy crown... every one of you will have just as many books to chew through and just as much misery to suffer."

"But I'll do everything I can. I'll teach you everything I know. I'll protect you and help you, right up until the day Mother and Father need one of you on that throne, and the best of you is ready for it."

"And when that day comes, I'll dash into my tree hollow, happy as anything, without stopping for a single second, and I will never come out again. You lot will leave everything I need at the entrance on a regular schedule, and then clear off as far as you possibly can."

...

Many years later, far from her homeland, Zvil and her people built a small new country that appears in no book anywhere.

Sometimes, on autumn afternoons, she would stare at a tree hollow and drift away into thought.

She always felt she had forgotten something. Of course she had. That black power had made everyone forget that country, and everyone who had stayed behind in that palace.

She had forgotten a princess named Vivian.

Vivian was the worst princess in the world. She was clever, elegant, and gracious.

Vivian was the best princess in the world. She was rude, lazy, and did whatever she pleased.

Vivian boiled herself down into a pot of soup.
